claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with: **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand Alex's current situation, as the rules differ for children aged 16 and over.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, staying in school, college, or an approved training program)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation and relationship with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you, or do you contribute financially to their upkeep?** (For example, paying for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your residency status.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 17 years old and still in college doing A-levels (which is approved education)
- Alex lives with you
- You live in the UK and are a UK citizen
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

This means you meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. Children aged 16-19 can still qualify for Child Benefit if they remain in approved education or training, and A-levels count as approved education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements because:
- You're responsible for Alex (living together)
- You live in the UK and are a UK citizen
- Alex is 17 and in approved education (A-levels)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Important things to note:**
- Your Child Benefit will continue as long as Alex stays in approved education or training and is under 20 years old
- If Alex leaves education or starts working 24 hours or more per week, your Child Benefit would stop
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the government website or by contacting HMRC.
